title: Urza Entrusts Tawnos with the War’s Testimony
summary: After the blast on Argoth, Urza charges his surviving apprentice to carry an account of their actions to other scholars.
narrative: After the catastrophe on Argoth, Tawnos emerged from his protective stasis and found that both the war and the landscape had changed. Urza told him that Mishra was dead and acknowledged the destruction their conflict had caused.

Urza directed Tawnos westward to the remaining scholars of the ivory towers so they would know what the artificers had done and failed to prevent. This assignment distinguishes the survival of testimony from the political reconstruction that Kayla later confronted.
Tawnos, the Toymaker is a retrospective portrait of the apprentice, not a literal illustration of Urza giving the instruction.
